messages:
Alex R: Quick sanity check — I'm about to push a tiny continuous-batching config change to cap max_batch_tokens at 48k and lower batch_window_ms to 12ms for the 8k prompt workload. Can someone run a quick throughput + tail-latency sweep on staging? I want to catch any p95/p99 regressions before merging. Config I'm going to push:
```json
{
  "continuous_batching": true,
  "max_batch_tokens": 48000,
  "batch_window_ms": 12,
  "min_batch_size": 2,
  "max_concurrency_per_gpu": 16
}
```
If you can run loadgen with the short prompt set (avg ~8k tokens) and paste tail numbers, that'd be great. Tagging @Priya.

Priya N: Ack, can run in ~15m. Which model variant? default quantized or fp16? Also want KV-caching warm or cold for this sweep?

Alex R: Default quantized (q4_0), warm KV please — that's our primary path in production.

Sam T: I'll do a quick perf probe as well. Noting that last sweep we saw ~6% throughput drop when window was 10ms. I'll compare numbers.

Len C: If you want reliable p99, run ~2m windows and an RPS ramp. I'll set up trace collector and post histograms. Proposal: fail the check if p99 > 250ms.

Maria V: FYI I noticed a weird p99 spike on staging yesterday — turned out to be a background snapshot job on cb-03. I'll make sure that is disabled on bench nodes.

loadbot: loadgen job started by Priya N on staging-cb-04. params: --model=q4_0 --seq=8192 --duration=120 --rps=200 --kv=warm

Priya N: Quick paste from the run: p50 34ms, p95 112ms, p99 238ms, throughput 195 rps. No obvious error logs, but host CPU spiked to ~72%.

Sam T: Mine (different node): p50 36ms, p95 120ms, p99 310ms — p99 noticeably worse. Attached top output snippet: ```
PID %CPU %MEM COMMAND
1234 71.2 2.3 ./inference_worker
```
Could be a Python helper thread or GC pause affecting the worker.

Alex R: Thanks. @Len can you correlate traces across those runs? I pushed a small allocator tweak to the batching code earlier — might be interacting with window alignment.

Len C: Pulling traces now... looks like one bucket of requests experienced an extra ~8ms queue delay before dispatch, probably due to misaligned batch window boundaries + a rare scheduler preemption. Suggest trying batch_window_ms = 16 to reduce jitter.

Priya N: Ran a quick follow-up with 16ms: p50 35ms, p95 108ms, p99 190ms, throughput 198 rps. Much better tail behavior.

Alex R: Sweet. Let's update the canary to 16ms and roll. I'll open a tiny PR and tag @Sam for CR.

Sam T: On it. I'll review the PR in ~1h. Also please add a unit/integration test for allocator stress to catch the queue alignment case.

Maria V: After merge can we add a nightly regression job that runs a 5-minute stable load and pushes metrics to the cb-dashboard? That should catch regressions early.

Alex R: Yep — opened PR #4822: https://git.redwood.ai/p/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4822 :thumbsup:

Priya N: Thanks all — I'll watch the canary rollout and post any anomalies here.

Len C: I'll add a short run to the tracing job to automatically flag p99 jumps > 30% vs baseline.

Sam T: Thanks — will add CR comments for the allocator test.

Alex R: Closing the loop: canary looks good after 30m, merging this afternoon unless someone objects. If you see anything odd ping here. :white_check_mark:
